dimension_grades.evidence: The document has no TL;DR or summary section; it opens with a multi-paragraph historical/philosophical introduction that contains no architectural decisions affecting caller behavior.
Fail-open vs. fail-closed behavior, retry semantics, and other non-obvious defaults are never mentioned anywhere in the document, let alone called out prominently.
There is no non-goals section anywhere in the document; the document only describes what the system will do, not what it explicitly will not do.

Decisions that constrain callers (e.g., domain-level authorization, descriptor model requirements) are buried in sections 6, 7, and 10, well after extensive historical context and philosophy in sections 1–3.

grades.criterion_name: Code examples as primary entry points

dimension_grades.evidence: The only code shown is a protobuf schema definition (server-side); no caller-side code in any real language (Go, Python, Java, etc.) is provided for any integration point.
No code examples use actual client libraries, middleware patterns, or production idioms; the only code is a protobuf definition with no client usage shown.
No code examples exist that demonstrate error handling or edge cases; the document contains no code beyond the protobuf schema and YAML configuration.
Neither the protobuf definition nor the YAML configuration example contains any inline comments explaining the 'why' of non-obvious lines.

grades.criterion_name: Concrete debugging artifacts in operational sections

dimension_grades.evidence: No exact gRPC status codes, HTTP response bodies, or error messages are shown anywhere in the document, including the security and monitoring sections.

Section 10 describes authorization rejection only from the server's perspective ('Attempts to check rate limits in a domain that the caller is not authorized to access are rejected') with no description of what the caller actually receives.
Section 11 mentions 'request volume, rejection rate, latency distribution, and current counter values' as dashboard panels but names no specific metric names, log field names, or trace attributes.
Section 10 mentions authorization rejection but provides no concrete example of a rejected request or the response a caller would receive.
Section 5 describes algorithm tradeoffs in neutral prose (e.g., 'higher memory usage,' 'boundary problem') but never explicitly flags any design decision as a tradeoff with a cost to callers.
No section identifies specific teams, use cases, or workflows that are negatively affected by any design decision; teams are only mentioned in historical context.
No workarounds or alternative approaches are offered for any constrained use case; the document presents all decisions as settled without escape hatches.
The document contains no admonition boxes, blockquotes used as callouts, or any visually distinct formatting to highlight tradeoffs; all content is uniform prose.
Section 5 compares three algorithms entirely in prose paragraphs with no table; performance characteristics in section 9 are also listed as prose sentences rather than a table.
No bold or emphasized text appears anywhere in the document body; all content is rendered in uniform weight prose.
Section 6 (API Design) references the domain concept without defining it, requiring readers to have read section 7; sections rely on prior context established in earlier narrative sections.
No callout or admonition boxes are used anywhere in the document; warnings such as the fixed window 'boundary problem' are embedded in plain prose paragraphs.
